A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSTA research. The complete documents, including equations, figures, tables, references, and v2's concluding limitations and pseudocode sections, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original video-recognition experiments, component and hyperparameter ablations, and latency/throughput measurements in Tables 2–8.

after.justification: v3 retains original recognition experiments and ablation results in Tables 2–6, and adds GFLOPs entries.

M1.justification: The shared multimodal adapter, spatial and temporal projections, frozen backbone, description-guided consistency loss, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Removing pseudocode does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Reported evaluations retain Kinetics-400, Kinetics-600, HMDB-51, UCF-101, and Something-Something V2 across the same four recognition settings. ActivityNet is mentioned in both introductions but has no reported evaluation in either PDF.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in recognition Tables 2–5 is unchanged. However, v2's separate ViCLIP-versus-MSTA latency/throughput comparison in Table 8 is removed, eliminating that specific baseline comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds GFLOPs as an evaluation metric in Tables 2–3 and removes the latency/throughput evaluation and its measurement procedure. Recognition settings, including Table 1 hyperparameters, backbone, shot counts, and frame/view protocols, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 removes the description-type ablation testing absent, spatial, and temporal descriptions (v2 Table 7), plus the empirical runtime analysis (Table 8). All six Table 6 ablations remain unchanged; the new description-count paragraph discusses an existing experiment.

E5.justification: v2 Section 4.1 explicitly states that Kinetics-600 results are averaged across three splits; v3 omits this aggregation information. Table 4 retains identical uncertainty values. Neither document establishes a change in runs or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Accuracy and uncertainty entries in Tables 2–6 are unchanged. v3 adds GFLOPs results, including 179.84 for MSTA versus 179.80 for AdaptFormer and LoRA. Removed results include Table 7's description ablations and Table 8's ViCLIP/MSTA latencies of 0.45/0.51 seconds and throughputs of 69.3/65.7 videos per second.

T1.justification: Equations 1–16 and their mathematical definitions are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved multimodal alignment and generalization through MSTA and description-guided consistency, strong performance across four settings, and training only 2–7% of original-model parameters. Rewritten abstract and conclusion wording preserves these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explicit limitation concerning suboptimal coupled visual/text backpropagation and interpretations accompanying the deleted description-type and runtime analyses. It adds a tentative explanation that increasing description count introduces more LLM hallucinations and noise, interpreting unchanged Table 6e results.

D1.justification: v3 removes Section 7 and Algorithms 1–2, losing explicit adapter construction, activation/dropout placement, and temporal convolution kernel, grouping, stride, and padding details. Detailed dataset/split specifications and runtime measurement instructions also disappear. Table 1, optimizer/hardware details, and the promised code-access information remain.

R1.justification: The same 44 cited works remain, and the related-work discussion retains its positioning against CLIP adaptation and unimodal transfer methods. Bibliographic back-reference changes reflect pagination rather than changed research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, early introduction, several ablation paragraphs, and conclusion. It removes duplicated method prose, merges abbreviated dataset descriptions into Experimental Setup, and deletes the limitations/broader-impact and pseudocode sections. Author affiliations and corresponding-author information also change.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 gain GFLOPs columns and revised formatting; Tables 7–8 and both algorithm displays disappear. Remaining tables are repositioned, Figure 1's grid changes, and schematic sizing/captions are adjusted. The core figure content and two-column presentation remain.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful GFLOPs comparisons and improves some prose, but removes implementation pseudocode, Kinetics-600 split/aggregation details, description-type ablations, runtime evidence, and a specific optimization limitation. These losses weaken reproducibility and scrutiny of the efficiency claims more than the editorial gains compensate. The unchanged method and main recognition results limit the overall decline.
